newsitem.title: USA: Vermont Yankee says nuke may start output Tues.
newsitem.headline: Vermont Yankee says nuke may start output Tues.

text.p: The 510 megawatt Vermont Yankee nuclear power plant in Vernon, Vt., may begin electricity production Tuesday pending a Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) review, a company spokesman said.

The NRC could complete a review of the plant's fire protection system by Monday evening, allowing the plant to restart Monday night and synchronize to the electricity grid on Tuesday, spokesman Rob Williams said Monday.
"They may complete their review today or tonight, we could then be in a position to restart tonight and be on line tomorrow," Williams said.

The plant was shut in early September for refueling and maintenance. Restart of the unit had originally been set for near Oct 24, but was pushed back by the NRC's request for more fire protection details.
"The plant itself is ready to go, (restart) depends on the NRC," Williams said.

Vermont Yankee is owned by a consortium of New England utilities including Central Vermont Public Service Co (31.3 percent), New England Electric System (20), Green Mountain Power (17.9) Northeast Utilities (16) and Central Maine Power Co (4.0).
